name: SK hynix Inc.
monetization: Sells HBM and server DRAM/NAND into the AI buildout — ~60% HBM share, lead HBM4 supplier to Nvidia, multi-year supply agreements with ~10 customers.
description_md: SK hynix is the leading high-bandwidth-memory (HBM) maker and the primary memory beneficiary of the AI super-cycle. HBM — stacked DRAM co-packaged with every AI accelerator — is one of the buildout's named bottlenecks, and SK hynix holds roughly 58–62% of the market with the lead position in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin generation (UBS estimates ~70% of Nvidia's 2026 HBM4 demand). Q2 2026 marked one of the most extreme quarters in semiconductor history: revenue ₩79.3T (+257% y/y) at a 76% operating margin. The company listed ADRs on NASDAQ in 2026.
ai_monetization_md: HBM3E/HBM4 sales to Nvidia, AMD, and ASIC programs, plus surging conventional server DRAM and enterprise NAND — all effectively sold out, with customers signing multi-year supply agreements (~10 customers) and prepaying in some cases (contract dollars undisclosed — a known data gap). Pricing power at the bottleneck produced a 76% operating margin in Q2 2026 (operating profit ₩60.5T, +557% y/y). SK hynix co-signed the OpenAI Stargate memory letter of intent with Samsung (Oct 2025): up to 900K DRAM wafers/month — roughly 40% of global DRAM output — earmarked through 2029.
ai_strategy_md: Defend the HBM lead across two generations simultaneously (HBM3E in volume, HBM4 ramped in 2026 with yields near HBM3E maturity; HBM4E samples shipped), add capacity on schedule (M15X fab wafer-in Q1 2026), and convert cycle windfalls into balance-sheet strength (net cash ₩69.4T) plus demand visibility via multi-year agreements. The Stargate LOI aligns it with OpenAI's buildout directly rather than only through Nvidia.
risk_notes_md: **Cyclicality:** a 76% operating margin is the strongest possible invitation for supply response (Samsung, Micron, and eventually CXMT) and for customers to design around HBM; memory has never sustained margins like this. **Customer concentration:** Nvidia dominates HBM demand; the Stargate LOI ties a large share of capacity to OpenAI's contested funding. **Commitment quality:** the LOI is a letter of intent, not a contract — headline wafer volumes are not booked revenue. **Korea/China exposure:** US export-control decisions on China fabs and equipment affect operations and the customer set.

observations.notes: +557% y/y; record 76% operating margin — the headline number of the memory super-cycle.
All-time high; net cash ₩69.4T after the NASDAQ ADR listing.
58% in Q1 2026 per Counterpoint (62% of shipments during 2025); UNIVERSE/SPEC cite ~58–60%. UBS forecasts ~70% of Nvidia's HBM4 demand in 2026.

events.title: Signs OpenAI Stargate memory LOI with Samsung — up to 900K DRAM wafers/month
events.why_it_matters: Earmarks ~40% of global DRAM output for OpenAI's buildout through 2029; an LOI, not a purchase contract, so it sits in the committed-but-unfunded tier until converted.

events.title: Q2 2026: revenue +257% y/y, 76% operating margin, HBM4 in mass production
events.why_it_matters: The clearest evidence that bottleneck ownership converts to pricing power; multi-year agreements with ~10 customers extend visibility, while the margin level itself raises supply-response and sustainability questions.

sources.notes: SK hynix projected to dominate Nvidia HBM4 demand.
